mutations.because: The budget shown while building must be the TIGHTEST html placement's (HL-D6): the smallest maxBytes is the profile that refuses first at packaging, so a meter reading the largest would promise a number one of the selected placements already breaks — the two-budgets disagreement this decision exists to remove.

Over budget the meter must say so with the overage (HL-D6): a builder whose unit already exceeds the placement budget has wasted work worth naming, and the refusal while building is the definition of done. Dropping the branch leaves the numbers on screen with nothing to distinguish a fit from an overage.

The weight reading is assembled once per change and shared: the meter (TemplateSection) and the overage (validateTemplateWarnings) both reach htmlWeightReading, so without the memo the whole unit is rebuilt and UTF-8 encoded on every keystroke, twice over. Dropping the cache read leaves the write in place but never served, so two identical calls assemble twice — the assemble-once test sees the second call reach the assembler.

The bare catch was the defect: it swallowed every error assembleHtml raises and hid the meter, so a real assembler bug looked like an unweighable draft. The fix checks the one expected failure (a missing or non-hex brand colour) up front and lets anything else propagate. Restoring the bare catch makes a stubbed assembler error disappear, so the propagate test — which asserts the throw reaches the caller — fails. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: VE3 added the per-tone loop and the `tones` cache key; The semantic edit is the same one; the after-text is that edit re-expressed against the current shape, not a new claim.)
